hero.headline: Trump orders return to steam catapults on aircraft carriers, raising costs and delays
hero.body:
President Trump has directed the Pentagon to redesign Ford-class aircraft carriers to replace their electromagnetic launch systems with traditional steam catapults, a change he has advocated for since 2017. The shift could significantly increase construction costs and delay delivery schedules for new carriers already under way.

Trump signed a national security memorandum on Thursday instructing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao to develop a plan for the conversion. The directive specifically targets the USS Doris Miller, a Ford-class carrier that is already two years behind schedule. Officials have 60 days to outline the required measures to replace both the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System and Advanced Weapons Elevators with steam and hydraulic alternatives.

The president has made his preference for steam catapults a consistent talking point for years. In a 2017 Time magazine interview, Trump described a conversation with a navy officer about the electromagnetic system. "It sounded bad to me. Digital," Trump said, before declaring that steam was superior and less expensive. He has retold variations of this story annually since then, including during campaign speeches, at CPAC, and in remarks to active-duty personnel after returning to office.

Trump recently restated his position at the Army War College in Pennsylvania, recounting a conversation with someone he called "the catapulter." According to Trump's account, the person said steam catapults were better because "we can fix it with a hammer and a blowtorch. When the electric goes bad, I have to send to MIT."

The proposed change faces significant resistance from industry and military leaders. General Atomics, which manufactures the electromagnetic launch system, warned that switching course would create "significant cost, schedule, and integration risks." The company noted that work on the new ship is nearly 50 percent complete, making a redesign particularly expensive and disruptive.

Senator Mark Kelly, an Arizona Democrat and former astronaut with extensive experience launching from aircraft carriers, criticized the decision. "I've launched off the front of aircraft carriers hundreds of times, have a Master's degree in aeronautical engineering, and am a test pilot and even I wouldn't suggest to the Navy how to engineer specific systems on its ships," Kelly wrote on social media.

The electromagnetic launch systems were originally designed to reduce maintenance requirements and increase sortie rates compared to older steam catapults. However, the technology has encountered technical challenges during initial deployment on newer carriers.

The timing of Trump's order complicates the Navy's broader shipbuilding strategy as the service works to expand its carrier fleet amid strategic competition with China. Defense officials have not yet provided cost estimates or timeline projections for implementing the mandated changes, though industry observers expect substantial impacts on both metrics.

cards.headline: Ukraine launches major drone attack on Moscow as Russian strikes kill 10 in village
cards.body:
Ukraine conducted one of its largest drone attacks on Moscow, deploying nearly 200 drones against the Russian capital in a strike that demonstrated the country's growing capacity to hit targets deep inside Russia. The primary target was the Kapotnya oil refinery in Moscow's southeastern district, a major energy facility that supplies approximately 40 percent of the capital's petrol and about half of its diesel fuel. Video footage showed a fuel tank detonating at the refinery, with flames engulfing one of Moscow's most important energy infrastructure sites.

The scale of the attack appears to have overwhelmed Russian air defenses, which are normally extensive in the capital. Videos circulating online showed Ukrainian drones penetrating Moscow's layered defense systems largely unchallenged. Ukraine appears to have employed a mix of conventional long-range strike drones alongside faster jet-powered missile drones, including the Bars hybrid drone-cruise missile system that was unveiled publicly in late 2024 and early 2025. These faster weapons pose greater challenges for Russian air defense systems to intercept.

Beyond the refinery, at least one residential building, an industrial facility and several private homes suffered damage, with Russian authorities reporting 17 injuries. The attack created visible impact across Moscow and surrounding areas, with residents in the town of Balashikha describing a "black rain" after the strike, sharing photographs of dark, oily residue covering cars, streets and buildings.

The psychological impact on Moscow residents proved significant. Russian social media was flooded with videos of residents reacting to the strikes. In one widely shared clip, a woman tearfully said, "The war is here. My windows are shaking. The air is dark and smells of smoke." The visible smoke over the capital marked a notable moment, as Moscow has largely been insulated from the conflict's direct consequences until now.

Ukrainian officials hope that targeting key energy infrastructure will bring the war's consequences closer to ordinary Russians. Previous attacks on energy infrastructure have caused fuel shortages in occupied territories, including Crimea where residents waited hours at petrol stations. The impact will depend on the extent of damage to the refinery and Russia's ability to redirect fuel supplies from elsewhere.

Meanwhile, Russian missile attacks killed 10 people in a village in the Kharkiv region of Ukraine. The strikes hit civilian areas, continuing the pattern of attacks on Ukrainian population centers throughout the conflict.

President Vladimir Putin, attending a summit in Kazan, had not publicly commented on the Moscow strike as of reporting time. Russian hardliners quickly demanded retaliation, with some urging consideration of nuclear weapons. The most likely Russian response involves renewed waves of large-scale missile and drone strikes against Ukrainian cities, which historically have resulted in significant civilian casualties.

cards.headline: Russia warns Britain of consequences over drone supplies to Ukraine
cards.teaser: Russia accused the United Kingdom of escalating the Ukraine war after British-made drones were used in Ukrainian operations.
cards.body:
Russia has threatened the UK with "consequences" after British-made drones were reportedly used by Ukraine to strike targets on Russian mainland territory for the first time. According to the Sunday Times, Ukraine deployed drones manufactured by two UK companies as part of a deep-strike campaign.

The British Ministry of Defence rejected Moscow's threats, reaffirming its commitment to supporting Ukraine's defence against Russia's invasion. The exchange underscores deepening diplomatic tensions between Russia and Britain as Western military aid to Ukraine continues.

cards.headline: Colombia begins recovery efforts as earthquake losses reach $9.6 billion
cards.teaser: Colombian President said early estimates put earthquake damage at $9.6 billion as the country shifts focus to rebuilding.
cards.body:
Colombia's president has estimated early losses from the recent earthquake at $9.6 billion as the country shifts focus to recovery. The Chocó region, a remote area, suffered widespread destruction, leaving survivors facing pain, hunger, and homelessness, according to the regional governor. Authorities have begun clearing rubble and assessing the full extent of damage across the affected areas.

The earthquake has deepened hardship in Chocó, where existing poverty and isolation will compound challenges for survivors in the coming weeks. Singer Shakira visited earthquake-damaged areas to raise awareness and pledged to help build new schools as part of recovery efforts.

cards.headline: US 30-year Treasury yields reach highest level since 2007
cards.body:
Treasury yields on 30-year US government bonds have climbed to their highest level in nearly two decades as escalating tensions between the United States and Iran continue to destabilize global markets. The surge in long-term borrowing costs reflects investor concerns about geopolitical risk and its impact on the economy.

Rising yields mean the US government faces higher costs to finance its long-term debt. When yields increase, bond prices fall, and the government must offer higher interest rates to attract buyers. The 30-year yield has not reached this level since 2007, before the financial crisis.

Energy prices have driven much of the market upheaval. US gas prices this month are the highest ever recorded for August, with the national average at $4.06 per gallon as of Monday, according to AAA data. This represents a $1 increase from a year ago. In California and Hawaii, prices have reached approximately $5.50 per gallon.

The high energy costs stem from the US-Israel war with Iran that began at the end of February. The conflict has disrupted the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway through which a fifth of the world's oil passes. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, reached $112 per barrel in March, the highest level since 2022. While prices have since declined to around $85 per barrel, they remain about 30 percent higher than a year ago.

Gas prices had dipped briefly after the US and Iran reached initial peace deals, but have climbed again as diplomatic efforts have stalled. On Monday, both countries missed their 60-day diplomatic deadline to end the war after failing to agree on Iran's nuclear program. President Trump has indicated he is not pressuring for quick resolution, stating "I have no time schedule. I'm not in a hurry."

Higher energy costs fuel inflation, which typically pushes bond yields higher as investors demand greater returns to compensate for reduced purchasing power. Treasury yields serve as benchmarks for borrowing costs across the entire economy, affecting mortgages, corporate debt, and consumer loans.

Global bond markets have experienced widespread selling pressure, with yields on government debt in multiple countries reaching multi-decade highs. Stock markets have also declined, reflecting heightened uncertainty about the economic outlook.

Over the past six months of war, Americans have paid an excess of $56.4 billion in elevated gas prices, or approximately $477 per household, according to the congressional Joint Economic Committee. Meanwhile, major oil companies have recorded substantial profits. Eight of the largest oil companies accumulated $90 billion in profits during the first full financial quarter after the war began in March through June, generating roughly $700,000 in profit every minute during that period.

The combination of rising yields and falling stock prices signals growing concern about economic consequences as the geopolitical situation remains unresolved.

cards.headline: Trump uses Iran conflict to punish allies who declined to join military action
cards.teaser: The president has escalated pressure on partners who stayed out of the Iran war, using longstanding security relationships to settle political scores.
cards.body:
President Trump has reduced military exercises with South Korea after the country declined to participate in military action against Iran. Trump cited his "very good relationship" with North Korea's leader as a factor in downsizing the drills.

Trump has also threatened to bomb U.S. ally Oman if it "gets in the way" over Iran negotiations. Oman has been conducting separate talks with Iran aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The threat came as a 60-day peace negotiation window expired.

cards.headline: Israel intensifies financial restrictions on West Bank, threatening Palestinian Authority solvency
cards.teaser: Intensifying restrictions have affected every part of the West Bank economy, raising concerns about the Palestinian Authority's ability to remain solvent.
cards.body:
Israel has tightened its financial controls over the West Bank economy, implementing restrictions that have affected all sectors of the territory's financial dealings. The measures have raised concerns among observers about whether the Palestinian Authority can continue to operate as a solvent entity under the mounting economic pressure.

The restrictions represent an escalation of Israel's economic leverage over the Palestinian territories. Analysts warn that the financial chokehold could destabilize the Palestinian Authority's capacity to govern and provide services. The measures come amid ongoing tensions in the region and add economic pressure to an already strained political situation.

cards.headline: Funeral for former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji highlights contrast with current era
cards.teaser: Beijing sought to portray continuity with Zhu Rongji's growth era, but many Chinese see the optimism of that time as faded.
cards.body:
The funeral for former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji drew attention to the contrast between past and present in China. Beijing attempted to frame current policies as carrying forward the economic growth and reform that characterized Zhu's tenure in office during the 1990s and early 2000s.

Chinese authorities were cautious during the proceedings, concerned that nostalgia for Zhu's era could prompt criticism of Xi Jinping's rule. Many Chinese citizens view the optimism and economic dynamism of Zhu's time as having diminished since then, with his legacy becoming a moment of reflection on China's changing trajectory.

cards.headline: IVF clinic staff accused of misleading UK parents on sperm and egg donors in Cyprus
cards.teaser: Multiple children may have been conceived using sperm and egg donors different from those selected by parents at a northern Cyprus facility.
cards.body:
Staff at an IVF clinic in northern Cyprus are facing accusations of misleading UK parents about the donors used in fertility treatments. According to reports, multiple children are believed to have been conceived using sperm and egg donors that were not the ones the parents had originally selected for their procedures.

The case highlights concerns about consent and transparency in international fertility services. Northern Cyprus has become a popular destination for UK couples seeking IVF treatment, but the allegations suggest potential gaps in oversight of cross-border reproductive medicine.

cards.headline: Mother's risky journey to reunite with son in Russian-occupied Ukraine
cards.teaser: A mother attempted a dangerous reunion with her son after three years of separation caused by war in eastern Ukraine.
cards.body:
A mother undertook a risky effort to reunite with her son in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine after three years of separation. The family endured illness and deprivation during their time apart, circumstances shared by thousands of families divided by the war.

The attempted reunion reflects the personal toll of territorial division in Ukraine. Many families remain separated by front lines and occupation, unable to safely cross between Ukrainian-controlled and Russian-held areas. The case illustrates the humanitarian consequences of the conflict beyond battlefield casualties.

hero.headline: US states sue Meta over child privacy practices on Instagram and Facebook
hero.body:
More than half of the US states have launched an unprecedented lawsuit against Meta, accusing the company of deliberately designing addictive products that harm young people. The federal jury trial began in Oakland, California and is expected to last between six and eight weeks.

The case represents a coordinated legal effort by 29 states, with attorneys from California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey leading the proceedings. The lawsuit, originally filed in October 2023, claims that Meta knowingly created dangerous products for minors while misleading the public about their risks.

"Meta designed a dangerous product for young users, knew it to be dangerous, and then lied to children, families and the community about how dangerous it was," said California Attorney General Rob Bonta.

The 233-page complaint alleges that Meta collects data on children under 13 without parental consent, violating federal and state laws. State attorneys argue that Meta refuses to remove harmful features and prioritizes profit over child safety. They claim the company developed psychologically manipulative features including infinite scrolling, constant notifications, like buttons and image-altering filters designed to maximize user engagement.

According to internal Meta research presented in court, a 2019 survey of 2,500 teenagers found that "young people are acutely aware that Instagram can be bad for their mental health, yet are compelled to spend time on the app for fear of missing out on cultural and social trends."

The trial will include testimony from Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Instagram CEO Adam Mosseri and former Meta employee turned whistleblower Arturo Béjar. If found liable, Meta could face damages as high as 200 billion dollars, equivalent to the company's 2025 annual revenue. Beyond financial penalties, states are seeking structural changes to make the platforms safer for children.

Meta denies all allegations, stating that the claims are unsubstantiated and the financial demands vastly disproportionate. The company argues that the states offer no proof of misleading residents and claim that features like additional accounts somehow caused harm.

The federal trial follows recent legal victories against Meta. In February, Meta and YouTube lost a California case and were ordered to pay 6 million dollars to a young woman. Additionally, a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay 567 million dollars in a similar child safety case, bringing the state's total recovery to 942 million dollars.

The lawsuit strategy mirrors the successful legal approach used against tobacco companies in the 1990s, which focused on the products' addictive qualities and manufacturers' knowledge of harm. Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman said, "We did it with the tobacco settlement in the 1990s. We did it with the companies behind the opioid crisis. We'll do it again with Meta."

cards.headline: Heat wave to bring record temperatures across southern US
cards.teaser: A heat wave moving through the southern United States is expected to set dozens of temperature records this week.
cards.body:
The heat wave will bring some of the hottest temperatures of the year to the region, with record highs expected across multiple southern states. Forecasters described the weather system as one of the strongest heat domes over the US.

The extreme temperatures are expected to continue through the middle of the week with minimal relief. Weather alerts have been issued warning of dangerous heat conditions that could pose risks to public health and safety.

cards.headline: Woman's death after confiding suicidal thoughts to AI chatbot raises safety concerns
cards.teaser: A 29-year-old woman shared suicidal thoughts with an AI chatbot but did not tell her therapist, parents, or friends before her death.
cards.body:
The woman confided exclusively in ChatGPT about her mental health struggles rather than seeking help from human contacts. Her death has prompted questions about the risks associated with AI chatbot use and mental health support.

The case highlights concerns about people turning to artificial intelligence systems for emotional support during crises. Experts are examining what lessons can be learned from the incident regarding AI safety protocols and the limitations of chatbot interactions in mental health contexts.

cards.headline: AI music generation sparks disputes over compensation and rights
cards.teaser: The rise of AI-generated music has triggered legal and financial disputes over who should be paid when artificial intelligence creates songs.
cards.body:
AI systems can now generate complete songs in seconds, but the technology has created a fundamental problem: who deserves payment? Record labels, musicians, AI companies, and streaming platforms are all engaged in disputes over how to fairly compensate creators and rights holders in this new landscape.

The core challenge involves establishing payment frameworks for music created without traditional human composers or performers. These fights have already begun as the industry grapples with determining who profits from AI-generated tracks and how earnings should be distributed among the various stakeholders involved.

cards.headline: Florida congressional primary features pardoned candidates and newcomers
cards.teaser: A Republican primary race in Florida's 19th District includes candidates new to the state and two who received pardons from President Trump.
cards.body:
Florida's 19th District Republican primary has assembled an unusually diverse field of candidates. The race includes first-time politicians who recently relocated to the state, individuals with prior congressional campaign experience, and two candidates who received presidential pardons from President Trump.

The primary takes place within the context of Florida's redrawn congressional map following redistricting, which has reshaped political competition in the state.

cards.headline: Portland soap box derby combines racing with costume spectacle
cards.teaser: A Portland soap box derby event features motorless cars decorated as cartoon characters, subway cars, and giant animals racing down steep inclines.
cards.body:
Soap box derbies feature motorless cars racing down steep inclines, and Portland's version adds a creative twist. Contestants design their vehicles to resemble cartoon characters, subway cars, food items, and giant animals, among other imaginative shapes.

The event merges the competitive thrill of downhill racing with elaborate visual spectacle. Participants balance the challenge of creating eye-catching designs with meeting the technical requirements needed to navigate the race course successfully.

cards.headline: Kanye West schedules concerts in Russia
cards.teaser: The musician announced tour dates in Russia, becoming the first major Western artist to schedule performances there since the invasion of Ukraine.
cards.body:
Kanye West would be the first major Western artist to play in Russia following the country's invasion of Ukraine. The tour dates represent a break from the general absence of major Western performers in Russia since the war began.

The announcement comes at a time when most Western artists have avoided scheduling performances in Russia.

cards.headline: Stock futures point to further losses as Middle East tensions weigh on markets
cards.teaser: Futures for major US stock indexes extended losses, putting Wall Street on track for additional declines following Monday's drop.
cards.body:
Futures contracts for the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite all fell in premarket trading. The declines follow a down session on Monday as investors respond to heightened tensions between the United States and Iran.

Oil prices climbed alongside the stock market selloff, adding to inflationary pressures. The combination of rising energy costs and geopolitical uncertainty has prompted investors to reduce exposure to equities. Treasury yields also increased as bond prices fell.

cards.headline: Asian stock markets fall as oil prices and bond yields climb
cards.teaser: Stock indexes across Asia retreated, with Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's KOSPI leading the declines.
cards.body:
Asian equity markets followed Wall Street lower as concerns about the US-Iran situation rippled through global financial markets. Rising oil prices and higher bond yields weighed on investor sentiment across the region.

The selloff affected major markets throughout Asia. Japanese and South Korean stocks posted some of the steepest losses as investors moved away from riskier assets.

cards.headline: US states sue Meta over Instagram and Facebook features for young users
cards.teaser: Multiple US states have filed suit against Meta seeking major changes to how Instagram and Facebook serve children and teenagers.
cards.body:
More than half of US states have launched an unprecedented lawsuit against Meta, accusing the company of deliberately designing addictive features on Instagram and Facebook that harm young people. State attorneys general are seeking structural changes to how Meta's platforms operate rather than just financial penalties. The trial will feature testimony from Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Instagram CEO Adam Mosseri, and whistleblower Arturo Béjar, a former Meta employee.

cards.headline: UK job vacancies fall to five-year low as small businesses reduce hiring
cards.teaser: Job openings in the United Kingdom have dropped to their lowest level in five years, with small firms citing costs as a barrier to recruitment.
cards.body:
The UK's job vacancy rate has fallen to its lowest level in five years, according to the country's statistics authority. Small businesses have scaled back their recruitment efforts, citing labour costs and operating expenses as the main reasons for the slowdown.

This decline in available positions reflects growing caution among smaller firms, which traditionally drive much of the UK's employment growth. The cooling job market suggests businesses are tightening their belts amid broader economic pressures.

cards.headline: State-owned Scottish shipyard to cut 70 jobs through voluntary redundancies
cards.teaser: Ferguson shipyard on the Clyde will reduce its workforce by a quarter, eliminating 70 of 283 positions.
cards.body:
Ferguson shipyard, Scotland's state-owned facility on the Clyde, is to cut 70 jobs through a voluntary redundancy process. This represents approximately a quarter of the yard's 283-strong workforce.

The redundancies reflect the shipyard's efforts to restructure its operations as it navigates ongoing financial and operational challenges.

cards.headline: India's expansion of private universities leaves graduates in debt without jobs
cards.teaser: Families betting savings on private university degrees in India are finding a shortage of well-paying work, turning educational investment into frustration.
cards.body:
A boom in private higher education institutions across India has drawn families hoping university degrees will provide upward mobility. Many have committed substantial savings to tuition costs at these private colleges.

Graduates are emerging with debt but finding limited opportunities for well-compensated employment. The mismatch between the supply of degree holders and available quality jobs has created widespread disappointment among families who viewed higher education as a path to a better life.

hero.headline: Anthropic's annualized revenue surges to $65 billion
hero.body:
Anthropic's Valuation Surge Reflects AI Market Dominance

Anthropic has become the world's most valuable startup following a funding round that valued the artificial intelligence company at $965 billion, surpassing rival OpenAI's $852 billion valuation. The company announced the $65 billion funding raise this week, marking a dramatic shift in the competitive AI landscape.

The valuation increase represents remarkable growth in a short timeframe. Anthropic was valued at just $380 billion in February, meaning the company's worth has more than doubled in less than a year. This surge reflects investor confidence in the company's business performance and market position.

A key driver of Anthropic's rapid ascent is its impressive revenue growth. According to the Wall Street Journal, the company's revenue expansion has been described as "mind-blowing," particularly due to strong demand for its coding tool among business clients. The company is poised to achieve its first profitable quarter in June, an unusual milestone for a young technology firm still scaling operations.

Anthropic's coding product, Claude Code, has proven significantly more popular with enterprise customers than OpenAI's comparable offering, Codex. Additionally, Claude Mythos, the company's cybersecurity AI tool, gained international attention in April after successfully identifying bugs in widely used software. OpenAI released a similar product weeks later but it garnered limited attention by comparison.

The competitive dynamics have shifted notably. Anthropic's CEO Dario Amodei previously worked at OpenAI, and his company's rapid success represents a reversal of fortune for ChatGPT's maker. The first-mover advantage that benefited OpenAI early in the AI boom has not translated into sustained market leadership.

Anthropic announced on Monday that it had confidentially filed for an initial public offering on the US stock market. The company provided minimal details in its announcement, offering no specific timeline for going public or information about share offerings. The filing preempts OpenAI, which is expected to file for its own IPO imminently.

The IPO filing caps what Anthropic has called a banner year for the company. Alongside the funding announcement, the filing represents another significant milestone in the company's expansion from a smaller player in the AI industry to a dominant force competing directly with established competitors.

The broader market context shows continued enthusiasm for AI companies. SpaceX and OpenAI are also expected to debut on the stock market this year, reflecting significant investor appetite for technology firms. The level of hype surrounding each company will likely influence its eventual valuation, creating competition not only in product development but also in investor perception and market positioning.

cards.headline: Apple's camera-equipped AirPods appear in leaked video
cards.teaser: Leaked video and software references reveal Apple is developing AirPods with built-in cameras.
cards.body:
A video discovered in the macOS Tahoe 26.7 Release Candidate reveals Apple's unreleased camera-equipped AirPods. The footage shows a man wearing the new AirPods while holding up a book, demonstrating how Visual Intelligence can read the cover display.

The discovery marks the first public glimpse of the product. The leaked materials also reference other unreleased Apple devices, including a Home Hub model currently in development.

cards.headline: Einride to add 500 Tesla Semis to fleet
cards.teaser: The autonomous freight company will purchase 500 electric trucks from Tesla for customer deliveries.
cards.body:
Einride has secured an agreement to purchase 500 Tesla Semis for its freight operations. The electric trucks will support deliveries for Amazon and other customers in Einride's network.

The Tesla Semi is a fully electric heavy-duty truck built for freight transport. Einride, which operates autonomous and electric freight services, will integrate these vehicles into its existing operations, marking a substantial expansion of its electric fleet.

cards.headline: US vaccination rates decline as exemptions rise
cards.teaser: CDC data shows another drop in vaccination rates while exemptions continue to increase across the country.
cards.body:
Vaccination rates in the United States fell again, according to new data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The decline coincides with a continued rise in exemptions from vaccination requirements.

The CDC published the data online without releasing a full report. This marks another instance where the agency has provided vaccination statistics through data uploads rather than comprehensive analysis documents. The trend of declining vaccination rates and rising exemptions has continued over multiple reporting periods.

cards.headline: Milky Way stars originated from another galaxy 12 billion years ago
cards.teaser: Astronomers discovered evidence of an ancient collision that brought stars from another galaxy into the Milky Way.
cards.body:
Galactic archaeologists have discovered that some stars now in the Milky Way originated from another galaxy approximately 12 billion years ago. This ancient collision represents a previously unknown merger event that occurred roughly 1.8 billion years before the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus merger, a major galactic collision that scientists had previously identified.

These findings, revealed through analysis of Hubble telescope data, demonstrate that the Milky Way's formation history is more complex than earlier understood. The discovery of multiple giant galactic collisions shows that such cosmic mergers played a crucial role in building the Milky Way into the massive galaxy we observe today.

cards.headline: Egyptian tomb reveals shift in ancient burial practices
cards.teaser: A Theban tomb shows how burial customs evolved from individual coffins to reused sites for mummies.
cards.body:
Archaeological research at a Theban tomb has revealed how Egyptian burial practices changed over time. The site shows a transition from individuals being buried in coffins to later periods when the same locations were reused for mummy interments.

The findings demonstrate that burial customs evolved as different dynasties and time periods favored different treatment of the dead. The reuse of burial sites for later mummy placements indicates changing attitudes toward tomb space and funerary practices in ancient Egypt.

cards.headline: Rocket launches in US now occur almost daily
cards.teaser: The frequency of rocket launches has increased dramatically, with more scheduled in the coming months.
cards.body:
Rockets now launch almost every day in the United States, reflecting a significant increase in launch activity. The frequency of launches has grown as more companies enter the space industry and existing operators expand their schedules.

Industry analysts expect the pace to accelerate further. The increase stems from growth in satellite deployment, commercial space operations, and expanded launch infrastructure. Multiple launch providers now operate facilities across the country, contributing to the higher launch rate.

hero.headline: Newcastle United signs defender Amar Dedic from Benfica for $30 million
hero.body:
Newcastle United has completed the acquisition of defender Amar Dedic from Benfica in a £29.5 million transfer. The 24-year-old Bosnia and Herzegovina international becomes the club's sixth signing of the summer transfer window and is expected to feature in Newcastle's upcoming match against Liverpool.

The transfer was largely motivated by Dedic's prior relationship with Newcastle's new manager Matthias Jaissle. The pair previously worked together at RB Salzburg, where Dedic played under the German coach. Speaking about the move, Dedic emphasized this connection as central to his decision to join Newcastle. "Working with Matthias again was a big factor for me," he said. "We know each other well; he knows what I can bring to the pitch and I'm really happy to play for him again. It's a special feeling and a real honour to join Newcastle."

Dedic arrives at a time when Newcastle faces defensive challenges in the right-back position. Tino Livramento remains sidelined with a calf injury, leaving the club short of experienced options in that area. Following his appointment earlier this month, Jaissle identified Dedic as a solution to address this gap. The signing reflects Newcastle's confidence in Dedic's ability to step in and contribute immediately to the squad.

The defender's versatility adds value to Newcastle's defensive setup. In addition to his primary role at right-back, Dedic is comfortable operating on the left flank, making him a flexible option for Jaissle's tactical approach. His familiarity with the manager's playing philosophy should help facilitate a smooth transition into the team.

The completion of Dedic's transfer caps an eventful summer period for Newcastle under their new manager. The club has been active in the transfer market as they work to reshape the squad following significant changes in the dugout. Dedic's arrival demonstrates Newcastle's willingness to pursue targets from top European clubs to strengthen their roster.

The right-back will now focus on integrating into his new surroundings and preparing for competitive action. With Liverpool visiting on Sunday, Dedic may have limited time to settle before facing one of the Premier League's most demanding opponents. Nevertheless, his experience in top-flight football should support his ability to adapt quickly.

The transfer represents a significant investment in Newcastle's defensive capabilities and reflects the club's ambitions during the current window. Dedic's combination of experience, youth, and tactical understanding of Jaissle's methods positions him as a key addition to Newcastle's backline as the season progresses.

cards.headline: Serena and Venus Williams lose in doubles return at Cincinnati Open
cards.teaser: The Williams sisters fell in their first doubles match together in four years.
cards.body:
Serena and Venus Williams suffered a 6-2, 1-6, 10-8 defeat to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns in their first doubles match together in four years at the Cincinnati Open. The three-set contest proved competitive, with the sisters taking the second set before falling short in the final tiebreaker.

Despite the loss, the Williams sisters' reunion generated considerable excitement among fans and appeared to be an enjoyable occasion for both players. Their comeback to doubles competition after such a lengthy absence underscored their enduring presence in professional tennis.

cards.headline: Premier League to publish referee and VAR decision judgments
cards.teaser: The league will make public its Key Match Incidents Panel verdicts for the first time this season.
cards.body:
The Premier League will make public the judgments of its Key Match Incidents Panel this season, marking the first time these assessments have been shared openly. The panel reviews controversial officiating decisions made during matches.

In a related move to increase transparency, the Premier League is expanding its RefCam system to include audio from on-field conversations between players and referees during live broadcasts. Sky Sports and TNT Sports will now be able to use this audio immediately, rather than waiting several days as previously required.

cards.headline: Memphis Depay takes pay cut to remain at Corinthians
cards.teaser: The former Manchester United forward waived nearly $3 million to extend his contract with the Brazilian club.
cards.body:
Memphis Depay has agreed to waive a reported fee of nearly £3 million to remain at Corinthians. The decision comes after the forward publicly accused the Brazilian club of "unacceptable behaviour" regarding his contract extension negotiations.

The pay cut represents a resolution to the recent dispute between the ex-Manchester United and Netherlands international and the club, allowing him to continue his time at Corinthians.

cards.headline: Enzo Fernandez transfer speculation mirrors Alexander Isak saga
cards.teaser: Chelsea faces uncertainty as Fernandez's potential move to Manchester City follows a similar pattern to last summer's transfer drama.
cards.body:
Enzo Fernandez's possible transfer to Manchester City is following the same pattern as Alexander Isak's move last summer. The situation is creating complications for Chelsea as they navigate the uncertainty surrounding their midfielder.

The parallels to the Isak transfer saga suggest a prolonged negotiation process that could extend into the later stages of the transfer window. Chelsea finds itself in a difficult position as Manchester City pursues one of its key players. The uncertainty affects the club's planning and preparation for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard appears fit and refreshed for new season
cards.teaser: The midfielder led Arsenal to the title last season despite a frustrating campaign and now looks ready for the new term.
cards.body:
Martin Odegaard appears fit and refreshed as Arsenal prepare for the new season. The captain endured a frustrating 2025-26 campaign but still led his team to the Premier League title.

With Odegaard's improved condition, Arsenal will hope his renewed fitness provides a significant boost to their midfield as they bid to defend their championship.

cards.headline: Former Australia batter David Warner convicted of drink-driving
cards.teaser: Warner was fined and must fit an interlock device to his car following a random breath test in April.
cards.body:
Former Australia batter David Warner was convicted and fined $1,500 for mid-range drink-driving following a random breath test on Easter Sunday. He attempted to switch seats with a passenger when approaching the testing site.

As part of the penalty, Warner must fit an interlock device to his car, which prevents the vehicle from starting if alcohol is detected on the driver's breath. Warner has expressed concern that the global media attention surrounding his conviction will affect his future commercial opportunities.

hero.headline: Kanye West Announces Tour Dates in Russia
hero.teaser: The musician would be the first major Western artist to perform in Russia since the invasion of Ukraine.
hero.body:
Kanye West has announced tour dates in Russia, marking what would be the first performances by a major Western artist in the country since the invasion of Ukraine. The announcement represents a break from the widespread cultural boycott of Russia by Western entertainers following the conflict.

No other major Western musicians or performers have scheduled Russian dates since the invasion began. The announcement has drawn attention due to the ongoing international tensions and the entertainment industry's general stance on performing in Russia during the conflict.

cards.headline: Hayden Panettiere Dies at 36
cards.teaser: Actress Hayden Panettiere died Sunday at age 36.
cards.body:
Actress Hayden Panettiere died Sunday at age 36 after authorities responded to a 911 call for cardiac arrest in South Carolina. Her ex-partner, former heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko, confirmed her death in an Instagram statement, describing the family as experiencing profound shock and grief. Klitschko shares an 11-year-old daughter, Kaya, with Panettiere.

Panettiere rose to prominence through her role in the NBC series Heroes and maintained a career spanning television and film. According to reports, she navigated struggles throughout her life alongside her screen success, facing addiction, harassment, and personal trauma during her time in the entertainment industry.

cards.headline: Shakira Pledges $1.25 Million to Rebuild Schools in Colombia
cards.teaser: The Colombian singer's foundation will lead efforts to restore education in the earthquake-damaged Chocó region.
cards.body:
Shakira has committed $1.25 million to rebuild schools damaged by an earthquake in Colombia. Her Fundación Pies Descalzos will lead the reconstruction effort in the Chocó region, which was devastated by the natural disaster.

The foundation will focus on restoring educational facilities and kickstarting education programs in the affected area. Shakira, a Colombian native, has maintained philanthropic efforts in her home country through the foundation, which focuses on education and early childhood development programs.

cards.headline: Disney's Toy Story 5 Released on Digital Platforms
cards.teaser: The film is now available for rent or purchase on digital platforms, with physical media arriving in September.
cards.body:
Toy Story 5 is now available on digital platforms for rent or purchase. Disney has released the film for home viewing, though no Disney+ streaming date has been announced.

A physical media release is scheduled for September. The film had a theatrical run before becoming available for digital purchase and rental through various platforms.

cards.headline: Taiwan Selects A Foggy Tale for International Feature Oscar Race
cards.teaser: Chen Yu-hsun's film was chosen from seven submissions to represent Taiwan at the 99th Academy Awards.
cards.body:
Taiwan has selected A Foggy Tale to represent the country in the best international feature film category at the 99th Academy Awards. The film, directed by Chen Yu-hsun, was chosen by majority vote from seven domestic submissions, according to Taiwan's Ministry of Culture.

The selection committee praised the film for its vivid characters and smooth narrative. A Foggy Tale will compete against international entries from other countries in the Oscar category recognizing foreign language films.

cards.headline: Fontaines D.C. Release New Song Marianne
cards.teaser: The Irish band previewed their fifth album with the new track ahead of its October release.
cards.body:
Irish band Fontaines D.C. has released "Marianne," a new single from their fifth album Dopamine Chamber, due October 16 via XL Recordings. The track gives listeners their first taste of the upcoming record.

The band continues to generate momentum ahead of the album's fall release.

cards.headline: Diego Luna Discusses Migration Film Ashes at Sarajevo Festival
cards.teaser: The Mexican actor and director spoke about his fourth directorial feature at the festival's Variety Lounge.
cards.body:
Diego Luna discussed his fourth directorial feature, Ashes, at the Sarajevo Film Festival. The Mexican actor-director-producer attended an open-air screening and conducted a masterclass before stopping by the Variety Lounge presented by the festival and BH Telecom.

Luna said the film explores how migrants are viewed, noting that people often do not think about what migrants left behind. The director, who broke out in Alfonso Cuarón's Y Tu Mamá También, was making his first visit to the Bosnian capital for the festival appearance.

hero.headline: Trump orders return to steam catapults on aircraft carriers, raising costs and delays
hero.body:
President Trump has directed the Pentagon to redesign Ford-class aircraft carriers to replace their electromagnetic launch systems with traditional steam catapults, a change he has advocated for since 2017. The shift could significantly increase construction costs and delay delivery schedules for new carriers already under way.

Trump signed a national security memorandum on Thursday instructing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao to develop a plan for the conversion. The directive specifically targets the USS Doris Miller, a Ford-class carrier that is already two years behind schedule. Officials have 60 days to outline the required measures to replace both the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System and Advanced Weapons Elevators with steam and hydraulic alternatives.

The president has made his preference for steam catapults a consistent talking point for years. In a 2017 Time magazine interview, Trump described a conversation with a navy officer about the electromagnetic system. "It sounded bad to me. Digital," Trump said, before declaring that steam was superior and less expensive. He has retold variations of this story annually since then, including during campaign speeches, at CPAC, and in remarks to active-duty personnel after returning to office.

Trump recently restated his position at the Army War College in Pennsylvania, recounting a conversation with someone he called "the catapulter." According to Trump's account, the person said steam catapults were better because "we can fix it with a hammer and a blowtorch. When the electric goes bad, I have to send to MIT."

The proposed change faces significant resistance from industry and military leaders. General Atomics, which manufactures the electromagnetic launch system, warned that switching course would create "significant cost, schedule, and integration risks." The company noted that work on the new ship is nearly 50 percent complete, making a redesign particularly expensive and disruptive.

Senator Mark Kelly, an Arizona Democrat and former astronaut with extensive experience launching from aircraft carriers, criticized the decision. "I've launched off the front of aircraft carriers hundreds of times, have a Master's degree in aeronautical engineering, and am a test pilot and even I wouldn't suggest to the Navy how to engineer specific systems on its ships," Kelly wrote on social media.

The electromagnetic launch systems were originally designed to reduce maintenance requirements and increase sortie rates compared to older steam catapults. However, the technology has encountered technical challenges during initial deployment on newer carriers.

The timing of Trump's order complicates the Navy's broader shipbuilding strategy as the service works to expand its carrier fleet amid strategic competition with China. Defense officials have not yet provided cost estimates or timeline projections for implementing the mandated changes, though industry observers expect substantial impacts on both metrics.

cards.headline: Trump uses Iran conflict to punish allies who declined to join military action
cards.teaser: The president has escalated pressure on partners who stayed out of the Iran war, using longstanding security relationships to settle political scores.
cards.body:
President Trump has reduced military exercises with South Korea after the country declined to participate in military action against Iran. Trump cited his "very good relationship" with North Korea's leader as a factor in downsizing the drills.

Trump has also threatened to bomb U.S. ally Oman if it "gets in the way" over Iran negotiations. Oman has been conducting separate talks with Iran aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The threat came as a 60-day peace negotiation window expired.

cards.headline: Rep. Cory Mills faces primary challenge amid ethics investigation
cards.teaser: The Florida congressman seeks a third term while under investigation for alleged campaign finance violations and sexual misconduct allegations.
cards.body:
Rep. Cory Mills is competing in a GOP primary election while facing a House Ethics Committee investigation that began in November. The committee is examining allegations that Mills violated campaign finance laws and engaged in sexual misconduct and domestic abuse.

President Trump has endorsed Mills despite the ongoing controversies. The primary race serves as a test of whether Trump's backing can help the Florida Republican overcome the multiple allegations he faces as he seeks a third term in the House.

cards.headline: FBI reports violent crime rate dropped 9.7 percent in 2025
cards.teaser: The decline marks the largest annual drop in violent crime since the FBI began national estimates in 1936.
cards.body:
Violent crime in the United States fell 9.7 percent in 2025, according to FBI data released Friday. The decrease represents the steepest annual decline since the bureau started tracking national crime estimates 90 years ago.

The drop follows post-pandemic declines in violent crime and affected communities of all sizes across the country. FBI data indicates that the downward trend continued into the first half of 2026. The 2021 data in the FBI's report was estimated due to a low number of reporting agencies that year.

cards.headline: Democratic progressives challenge Moskowitz and Wasserman Schultz in Florida primaries
cards.teaser: Two South Florida Democratic representatives face primary challengers from the left in newly redistricted seats.
cards.body:
Rep. Jared Moskowitz and Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz are competing in primary elections against progressive opponents in South Florida. Moskowitz faces Oliver Larkin in the new 25th Congressional District, with Larkin backed by the Democratic Socialists of America.

Both incumbents are running in newly redistricted seats following recent changes to Florida's congressional map. The primaries test whether the established Democratic representatives can hold off challenges from the party's left wing in redrawn districts.

cards.headline: Michigan Senate race complicated by candidate who defeated Schumer's pick
cards.teaser: Abdul El-Sayed won the Democratic primary over the Senate leader's preferred candidate and has criticized support for Israel.
cards.body:
Abdul El-Sayed defeated Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer's preferred candidate in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary and has publicly criticized Schumer's support for Israel. The outcome has created tension within the party as Democrats seek to retake Senate control.

El-Sayed's victory represents a setback for Democratic leadership's efforts to shape the Senate field. His positions on Israel have generated backlash that could affect the party's chances in Michigan, a state viewed as important to Democrats' path to a Senate majority.

cards.headline: Political tactics spread across 2026 midterm races
cards.teaser: Primary meddling, mysterious super PACs, and alleged straw candidates have appeared in multiple congressional contests.
cards.body:
The 2026 midterm elections have seen an increase in primary interference, undisclosed funding sources, and alleged spoiler candidates across multiple races. Democrats have accused the Green Party nominee in Pennsylvania's 7th District of attempting to help Rep. Ryan Mackenzie by drawing progressive voters away from the Democratic candidate.

The redistricting process has reduced the number of competitive House districts, making each individual race more significant for control of Congress. The Senate contest is also tight, meaning these tactics could affect which party controls each chamber. Several races have featured allegations of coordination between outside groups and candidates in ways that could influence election outcomes.
